pr_body:

being written. Add the missing error handler.

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/37291

issue_context.title: investigate flaky test/parallel/test-http-many-ended-pipelines.js
issue_context.body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting a flaky test.

Flaky tests are tests that fail occasionally in the Node.js CI, but not
consistently enough to block PRs from landing, or that are failing in CI jobs or
test modes that are not run for every PR.

Please fill in as much of the template below as you're able.

Test: The test that is flaky - e.g. `test-fs-stat-bigint`
Platform: The platform the test is flaky on - e.g. `macos` or `linux`
Console Output: A pasted console output from a failed CI job showing the whole
failure of the test
Build Links: Links to builds affected by the flaky test

If any investigation has been done, please include any information found, such
as how consistently the test fails, whether the failure could be reproduced
locally, when the test started failing, or anything else you think is relevant.
-->

* **Test**: test/parallel/test-http-many-ended-pipelines.js
* **Platform**: macOS 10.14, macOS 10.15
* **Console Output:**
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2021 08:14:57 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
Keep-Alive: timeout=5
Content-Length: 2

ok
node:events:355
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^

Error: read ECONNRESET
    at TCP.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:211:20)
Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance at:
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:192:8)
    at emitErrorCloseNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:157:3)
    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:81:21) {
  errno: -54,
  code: 'ECONNRESET',
  syscall: 'read'
}
```
* **Build Links**: https://ci.nodejs.org/job/node-test-commit-osx/38908/nodes=osx1014/testReport/junit/(root)/test/parallel_test_http_many_ended_pipelines/
comments:
I'm able to replicate this locally with this command:

```
tools/test.py -j96 --repeat=1920 test/parallel/test-http-many-ended-pipelines.js
```

If I remove the `-j96`, I am unable to replicate it. So that suggests some sort of resource constraint (memory? CPU? network? file descriptors? *something*) makes the issue more likely to happen.

I know there's been some refactoring of streams and stream-like http/net events, and even some small breaking changes I believe. 

@ronag @lpinca Any idea if the bug here is in the test code or if it's probably indicative of a bug in Node.js core?
It seems to me that the test is flaky by design. The socket might be destroyed server-side while the client is still writing to it.
I think the test is missing a `'error'` handler. An ´ECONNRESET` looks like a expected/normal thing here.

The issue can be exacerbated by increasing `numRequests`. Setting it to 2000 makes the test always fail on my machine.

Also, there seems to be an unwanted `MaxListenersExceededWarning` caused by https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/33d3a2e6cb9004ecdd1413100c5b585744702b61/lib/_http_incoming.js#L180-L183. I think the condition here https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/33d3a2e6cb9004ecdd1413100c5b585744702b61/lib/_http_incoming.js#L178 should prevent `finished()` from being called again with the same `socket` argument.
@ronag, the second issue (the unwanted warnings) seems to be caused by https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/2da36112d177efc19201f1610dcf51647378131c. I'm not sure if it makes sense to revert it.

> @ronag, the second issue (the unwanted warnings) seems to be caused by [2da3611](https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/2da36112d177efc19201f1610dcf51647378131c). I'm not sure if it makes sense to revert it.

I don't think we should revert. I'll see if I can find a better solution.

I'm seeing this error in an application of mine on OSX 10.15.7, seemingly immediately after the client closes a websocket connection.
```js
GET /nats 2ms (unfinished)
node:events:355
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^

Error: read ECONNRESET
    at TCP.onStreamRead (node:internal/stream_base_commons:211:20)
Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance at:
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:188:8)
    at emitErrorCloseNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:153:3)
    at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:81:21) {
  errno: -54,
  code: 'ECONNRESET',
  syscall: 'read'
}
WARNING - child /Users/jameshilliard/.nvm/versions/node/v15.8.0/bin/node exited with code 1
```

TCP stream captures from wireshark below.

client->server:
```http
GET /nats HTTP/1.1

Connection: Upgrade
Pragma: no-cache
Cache-Control: no-cache

Sec-WebSocket-Key: QBAgXK0zfCKz/dMS6Pb6Sw==

```
server->client:
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Connection: close
content-type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8

Welcome to SockJS!
```

Any idea what's going on here or how to debug further?

@jameshilliard In a vanilla callback context, `try`/`catch` will catch thrown errors, not error events. Prior to `async`/`await`, `try`/`catch` was favored for synchronous errors and `error` events were emitted for asynchronous errors. Since you're not using `async`/`await`, those rules apply here.

Your issue is not related to the issue being discussed here. They have the same error code, but a connection reset can be caused by many, many things. I'm going to hide your comments as off-topic. If you need further help, I'd suggest opening an issue in [the SockJS repository[(https://github.com/sockjs/sockjs-node), [the help repository](https://github.com/nodejs/help) or on [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/).

> Your issue is not related to the issue being discussed here. They have the same error code, but a connection reset can be caused by many, many things.

Ah, I was assuming nodejs made some change that broke that particular sockjs code.

review_comments: I think `err.code` can also be `'EPIPE'` or `'ECONNABORTED'` but I was not able to reproduce. Should we handle that in advance or do it if/when it will occur?
I'd say let's do it when it occurs.
Perhaps you can add a comment right now that says "EPIPE might be valid too but we haven't seen it yet" or something like that?
